queries.hook: Being held to a timeline by the people who praise your work, and the shame of feeling you are failing a test you never agreed to take. My parents' expectations weigh on me.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A son or daughter who built a life their parents did not plan, questioned them openly, and found their footing in the truth they were given.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that a life lived by another's rules is a borrowed life. He says that doing your own work, even if it is flawed, is better than perfectly performing someone else's duty. The point is that your work should fit your own nature. You are not failing because you are imperfect. You are failing because you are wearing a mask that was never yours to wear. The shame you feel comes from trying to pass a test that was written by someone else.
verse.for_you: You are working those night shifts and sending money home because it is your nature to provide. You are not failing. You are simply trying to pass a marriage timeline that your parents set for you. Let your work be your offering, not your report card.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that no action is caused by a single person alone. Every act has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. To think you are the only one responsible for an outcome is to see only a fragment of the truth. This means you are not the sole author of your life's problems.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today, see that your parents' pressure is only one of the five causes shaping your life. You are not the sole author of your shame. You are one cause among many, and the outcome is not yours alone to carry.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

matched.label: I feel ashamed of who I am

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: In the forest, Draupadi is tired of hearing Yudhishthira wait on fate while they sit and suffer. She tells him that a person should never look down on himself, because the one who despises himself never finds real prosperity. She is saying that waiting for the world to fix itself is not a life. You do your part, then you work as if everything depends on you. That is how you stop being a prisoner of their expectations.
verse.for_you: They are proud of your money, but they use it to keep you in a box. You are not failing. You are doing the work, and you are still worthy. Let that be enough for today.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield and says that a person must raise themselves by themselves. Do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. He is telling Arjuna that the only constant is his own mind. He must choose to be his own ally instead of his own critic.
verse.for_you: When you are alone in the quiet after your shift, do not let the voice of their test become your own voice. You are your own ally right now. Let that be the truth you hold onto.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated on the ground, having lost his kingdom. She tells him he must not think less of himself or settle for little. He should set his mind on what is truly good and stop fearing. She urges him to pull himself together and rise. The idea is that past failure does not define you, and those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Your parents keep asking when you will marry, and you feel like you are failing a test they set. Vidula tells her son to stop thinking less of himself. You are not failing. You are building a life of your own, and that deserves your respect.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells his student Nidagha how a free person moves through the world. This person does the work that comes, speaks gently, and reads other people's hearts. By letting go of what is lost and taking up what comes, they do not sink in the world. They live fully but stay calm inside.
verse.for_you: Today, when your parents ask about marriage, do the work in front of you and speak gently. Let their words come and go without letting them pull you under. You can stay calm inside while you handle what is right in front of you.

story.title: Bharata wrongly blamed
story.story_hook: He had done nothing, and the one person whose good opinion he needed was sure he had done it all.
story.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.
story.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

anchor.speaker: Bharata
anchor.setting: Grieving Kausalya accuses Bharata of plotting Ram's exile; he knew nothing of it.
anchor.sanskrit: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥
anchor.line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.
anchor.translation: Noble lady, why do you blame me, who knew nothing and did nothing wrong? You know how deep my love for Ram is.
anchor.why: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

story.hook_title: Bharata had done nothing, and Kausalya was sure he had done it all
story.teaser: Bharata had done nothing, and Kausalya was sure he had done it all
story.for_you: You are sitting in the dark after your shift, and the phone rings with the question you dread. You do not have to take the blame for a life you did not choose. Show them your truth, gently but firmly. Your innocence is not a weakness. It is the ground you stand on.

script: You are carrying a weight that is not yours. You are working long night shifts, sending half your salary home, and you feel like you are failing a test you never agreed to take.

On the battlefield, Arjuna is paralyzed by grief. He tells Krishna that he will not fight, that he would rather die than kill his own kin. The armies stand ready to clash, and Arjuna has laid down his bow. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna says that your own path, imperfectly walked, is better than someone else's done perfectly. This is not about caste or family script. It is about honest fit. You are not failing because you are imperfect. You are failing because you are wearing a mask that was never yours to wear. The shame you feel comes from trying to pass a test that was written by someone else.
You are providing for your family. That is your work. Let it be your offering, not your report card. You do not have to wear the mask of the perfect partner to be worthy.
What if your own path was already enough?

depth.life: You are on the phone for hours after your night shift, answering your parents' questions about marriage while your own career feels buried. They praise your sacrifice but keep pressing the timeline you never agreed to take.
depth.points: The test they keep handing you is not yours. A life lived to please others is a borrowed life that leaves the self empty. Your own duty, done imperfectly, carries more truth than someone else's perfect script.
depth.practice: Name one thing today that is truly your own, not theirs. Write it down and let it sit.
depth.question: What is the one thing you would do if no one was watching?
